# Let configuration choose an initial condition

[Keep the mathematics in C++. Put the choice and its parameters in the input file.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The [pattern lesson](../patterns/index.qmd) passes a callable directly to
a field. A configurable application can instead create a `FieldModifier`
from a name. This refactoring of `10_ui_register_ic` uses OpenPFC's actual
catalog rather than maintaining an unrelated map of functions.

## Describe one new field

Our extension fills an affine function,

$$
u(\mathbf x)=b+a_xx+a_yy+a_zz.
$$ {#eq-affine}

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="modifier"}
```

The modifier receives a mutable host view, the physical domain and the
owned box. `pfc::field::apply` performs the coordinate traversal. This
keeps the formula independent of both the local array layout and the
application's configuration format.

## Register the constructor, then apply its result

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="catalog" dedent=4}
```

The catalog starts with built-in initial conditions and adds `affine`.
Its factory validates the supplied parameters and constructs the modifier.
An unknown name reports the registered choices. Every MPI process builds
its own catalog and applies its modifier to its own field.

This catalog is an ordinary local object. It does not mutate the
process-wide default catalog, and the modifier's mathematics does not
depend on registration. A larger JSON-driven session can perform the
same wiring for named simulation fields.

## Make a change without recompiling the physics

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
```

Change `offset` or `slope` in `initial_condition`. As a second experiment,
replace the whole object with `{"type":"constant","n0":0.4}`.
That selects a built-in modifier through the same catalog. Try an unknown
type and read the diagnostic instead of guessing what was selected.

The program writes the actual owned field to `results/fields_rank_*.csv`.
Both the affine and constant cases are checked globally on one and two
ranks. The default x/y interval is $[-4,4)$, so this affine profile is
not generally continuous across a periodic seam; this lesson fills and
inspects it without evolving a periodic PDE.

Keep the [model](model.cpp), [input](input.json) and
[shared helper](../lesson.hpp). Continue with
a native configuration-driven session.
:::
